title: Paint Calculator
metaTitle: Paint Calculator: Gallons of Interior Wall Paint Needed
metaDescription: Calculate how many gallons of paint you need for any room. Automatically deducts doors and windows with custom coats and coverage.

inputs.help: Standard ceiling height is 8 or 9 feet.

constants.label: Coverage per gallon (sq ft)
constants.note: Standard interior wall paint covers 350 to 400 sq ft per gallon. Textured or porous drywall may reduce coverage to 300 sq ft. Verify against the paint can label.

constants.label: Standard door deduction (sq ft)
constants.note: Standard 30 × 80 in door equals roughly 20 sq ft.

constants.label: Standard window deduction (sq ft)
constants.note: Average residential window equals roughly 15 sq ft.

content.intro: Refreshing an interior room with a fresh coat of paint is one of the most cost-effective home improvement projects, but running out of paint mid-wall or storing multiple unused cans creates unnecessary hassle. This free paint calculator estimates the exact gallons and whole cans required for any room, deducting standard doors and windows to determine true net wall surface area. Enter your room length, width, ceiling height, and desired number of coats below to get accurate purchasing recommendations based on standard gallon coverage, ensuring clean application without multiple trips to the paint store.
content.howItWorks: Room perimeter is calculated by adding length and width together and multiplying by 2. Multiplying perimeter by wall height yields gross wall area in square feet. Deductions are subtracted for openings: 20 square feet per standard interior door and 15 square feet per standard window. Net wall area is multiplied by the number of coats (typically 2 coats for uniform coverage and color saturation) and divided by paint spread rate (standard 350 sq ft per gallon). The result is rounded up to the nearest whole gallon can because retail paint is sold in full cans.

examples.title: A standard 14 by 12 foot bedroom with 8-foot ceilings
examples.text: For a bedroom measuring 14 × 12 ft with 8-foot ceilings, 1 door, and 2 windows receiving 2 coats: perimeter is 2 × (14 + 12) = 52 feet. Gross wall area is 52 × 8 = 416 sq ft. Subtracting 1 door (20 sq ft) and 2 windows (30 sq ft) leaves 366 sq ft net wall area. Applying 2 coats requires 732 sq ft of coverage. Dividing by 350 sq ft per gallon gives 2.09 gallons, meaning you should purchase 3 gallon cans.

examples.title: A 12 by 10 foot home office with 1 door and 2 windows
examples.text: Perimeter is 2 × (12 + 10) = 44 feet. At 8 feet high: 44 × 8 = 352 sq ft gross. Subtracting 1 door (20 sq ft) and 2 windows (30 sq ft) yields 302 net sq ft. For 2 coats: 302 × 2 = 604 sq ft. Dividing by 350 equals 1.73 gallons, requiring 2 one-gallon cans.

commonMistakes: Skipping primer over bare drywall or dark existing colors, which forces applying three or four topcoats.
Forgetting to deduct windows and doors, causing over-purchasing of expensive premium paint.
Trying to stretch a single coat over existing walls, resulting in thin coverage, flash marks, and roller streaks.
Not buying all paint cans in the same store batch or boxed together, which can cause subtle sheen and tint variations.

faq.q: How many square feet does one gallon of paint cover?
faq.a: One gallon of interior paint covers between 350 and 400 square feet on smooth, primed surfaces. On rough, unprimed drywall or heavily textured plaster walls, coverage drops closer to 250 to 300 square feet per gallon.

faq.q: Is one coat of paint ever enough?
faq.a: One coat is only sufficient when applying an identical color and sheen over an existing wall that is in good condition. When changing colors, painting over patches, or using darker shades, two coats are essential for uniform color depth and proper sheen.

faq.q: How do I calculate paint needed for the ceiling?
faq.a: Ceiling area is simply room length multiplied by room width. For example, a 12 × 14 foot room has a 168 sq ft ceiling. At 350 sq ft per gallon, one gallon covers two full coats on the ceiling.

faq.q: What should I do with leftover paint?
faq.a: Store a small sealed jar of leftover paint for future wall touch-ups. Label it with the room name, paint brand, color name/formula, and date. To dispose of larger amounts, mix with cat litter or paint hardener until solidified before disposal.
